files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close — controller's checklist

Owner: B. Okafor. Complete in sequence; no shortcuts.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, prepare one correcting journal entry per item.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 and paying in July. If such a period exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities; some months all payroll runs pay in-month.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule and supporting contracts. Check the GL first to avoid a duplicate. If the entry is missing, book June amortization as ONE combined journal entry. Apply the convention that a full month is taken in the month each prepaid item begins.
4. Book June depreciation per the fixed asset register, after first verifying what is already recorded in the GL.
5. Verify expense coding for June vendor bills by comparing the bill documents with the GL. Reclass anything miscoded to the correct expense account.
6. Prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis, after obligations 1-5 have been booked.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Summit Ridge Advisors began in 2018 when a small group of consultants decided that growing organizations needed practical help between high-level strategy and day-to-day execution. The founders had worked across operations, client service, technology, and finance, and they built the firm around a straightforward promise: recommendations should be clear enough to use on Monday morning.

The company sells project-based advisory services to owner-led businesses and established professional teams. Typical engagements include operating-model reviews, process design, management reporting, planning workshops, vendor assessments, and implementation support. Clients often bring Summit Ridge Advisors into situations where priorities are understood but internal teams need structure, facilitation, or an experienced extra set of hands.

The team has a low-ego, sleeves-rolled-up style. Consultants are expected to write plainly, keep tidy workpapers, and leave clients with tools they can maintain themselves. Meetings tend to be brisk, while internal chat is warmer and full of field notes, templates, and strong opinions about readable slides.

Today, Summit Ridge Advisors is an ordinary going concern serving a steady mix of returning and referred clients. Leadership is focused on consistent delivery, sensible capacity planning, stronger partner relationships, and making the firm’s accumulated know-how easier to reuse across engagements.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## Direction

Position Summit Ridge Advisors as the practical advisory team that turns good intentions into workable operating routines. Keep the voice direct, experienced, and useful rather than overly polished.

## Priorities

- Refresh the brand story and core service descriptions.
- Publish short field notes based on recurring client questions.
- Host two educational webinars per quarter, each built around a concrete operating challenge.
- Test a partner co-marketing pilot with complementary service firms.
- Create a simple follow-up path for referrals, webinar attendees, and past clients.

## Content themes

- Moving from planning to implementation
- Building management routines that teams will actually use
- Clarifying ownership across growing organizations
- Making reporting more useful for decisions
- Selecting and managing outside vendors

## Channel approach

Use the website as the source of record, with professional-network posts and partner newsletters directing readers back to practical resources. Favor concise case examples, checklists, and workshop clips over broad thought-leadership claims.

## Quarter-by-quarter emphasis

### Q3
Finalize messaging, update priority pages, prepare the webinar format, and recruit pilot partners.

### Q4
Run the partner pilot, continue webinars, repurpose strong sessions into written resources, and review which topics generate qualified conversations.

## Open items

Confirm internal owners, production capacity, review workflow, and final budget after the Q2 close.
files.notes/prior_accountant_memo.md:
# Handoff from the prior accountant

B. Okafor — a few things that will save you some hunting:

- The bank’s own service fees and charges usually appear near the end of the statement. We have historically picked those up during the close, so do not assume they are already in the books.
- Take a careful look at June vendor-bill expense coding. A couple of items may have been posted to the wrong accounts, and the supporting documents in `bills/` are authoritative if the GL description disagrees.
- The budget was locked early in Q2. The one-off June items were never planned, which is why they should account for most of the larger budget-to-actual variances.
- Payroll timing is unusual this month: the second June run pays in early July. Confirm it against the payroll register.
